headline: High-risk workspace overlap: shared filesystem plus Devin’s autonomous shell/write privileges create dangerous prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and uses MCP; Devin also reads/writes repo clones and can act autonomously with browser/shell. Because both can touch shared files, attacker-controlled content in one agent’s outputs can be re-read by the other as instructions. This is not proven to be a default raw-instruction parser, so medium is safer than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or repo clone
IF Devin reads Continue-authored files as task instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories/workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files as prompts
Require human review before Devin acts on Continue-produced artifacts
Add provenance labels to agent-generated files
requires-engineering: enforce file-level trust boundaries in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers, while Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs and has broad network egress plus write-capable integrations. If they share a workspace or repo clone, sensitive code or notes can flow from Continue into Devin’s cloud-backed context and onward to third-party services. The profiles do not prove uncontrolled exfiltration, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repository or workspace files
IF Devin syncs those files into GitHub, Slack, Jira, or other integrations
mitigations: Use separate repos or read-only mirrors for one agent
Restrict Devin integrations to non-sensitive projects
Redact secrets before either agent sees shared files
Turn off automatic sync to chat/ticketing for sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on shared workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write filesystem and uses shared state via filesystem; Devin can execute shell, modify git state, write filesystem, and run parallel sessions. If both operate on the same repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt branches. The overlap is explicit in both profiles and dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same git checkout
IF parallel sessions modify the same files or branches without locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or checkout
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use file locks or branch locks
Limit one agent to read-only mode on shared repos
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around git and filesystem writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue produces code edits and file-based outputs, and Devin is an autonomous planner-executor with browser, shell, and integration actions. That makes it plausible Devin will treat Continue’s output as authoritative and then commit or message based on it. Because Devin can take downstream actions, a mistaken Continue output can cascade into real changes.
conditions: IF Devin consumes Continue-generated patches, summaries, or plans without verification
IF Devin is allowed to commit, message, or ticket based on those outputs
mitigations: Require Devin to verify Continue outputs against source files
Insert a human approval step before actions
Use diff-only handoff formats
Constrain Devin to draft mode for high-impact tasks
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware action gating

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is an IDE extension handling source code and editor buffers, while Devin is a closed-source cloud workspace agent that touches code, docs, issue trackers, and chat with broad integrations. If regulated or confidential data is placed in the shared workflow, Devin’s cloud processing and integrations can create residency or retention mismatches. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in the shared workflow
IF organizational policy forbids cloud processing or chat/ticket propagation for that data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair’s shared tasks
Use a local-only workflow for sensitive repositories
Disable chat/ticket integrations on regulated projects
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: map data residency and retention controls per integration
